task: Use the optional shared records: take a published toolchain set into a home, or publish one from CI
do: Off unless chosen: with no `--origin`, blaze contacts nothing and a new checkout is served by the machine's own content-deduplicated store. To take a set: `--origin <url|folder>` (with `--origin-key <hex>`, the Ed25519 public key trusted for it) on `blaze check` or `blaze warm-toolchain` (build, run and test take them too) takes this blaze's toolchain-and-target set into the home's store before the first phase, its head checked against a trusted key; then every record is a local hit (crates/blaze-cli/src/store/take.rs). To publish (a trusted builder: a blaze built with blaze-cli's `publish` feature, CI's): `blaze store publish <folder> --signer <key file>`, the key file holding the Ed25519 seed as 64 hex digits (`openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -outform DER | tail -c 32 | xxd -p -c 64`); a developer's blaze refuses it by name, and an http(s) origin is refused for everyone. crates/blaze-remote's bucket push and pull (`cmd.rs`, the `BLAZE_CACHE_*` settings) are built and not wired into the CLI. Tests: `blaze test -p blaze-remote` (the fake bucket; nothing contacts a service).
why: The flags, who may publish and the off-by-default origin are spread over take.rs, publish_command.rs and the CLI spec; this is the one place that says how to use them.
